design.summary:
A1: implement. A5: implement smaller than proposed. I built both as a prototype in a scratch copy under /private/tmp (the repo is untouched). It runs green, and its patches are the starting point for the real edit.

A1 (ids refusal). When a declared ID is missing from the runner output but appears only inside a longer token, the refusal now says so. Today the text says "Make the command select those cases and print test names (for example --verbose)". That is wrong in the Checkers case, because node had already printed `✖ TC-4a ...`.
- `shiploop_test_counts.named` returns a new key `inside`: missing ID -> first non-skip output line containing it, cut to 100 characters.
- `shiploop_test_loop.judge` copies it into the verdict as `ids_inside`, only when non-empty.
- The `ids-missing` branch of `shiploop_test_loop._explain` leads with the rule and the line. Run against the real Checkers output, it prints: `did not show TC-4, TC-6, ... as a whole word (node reported 27 run, 27 failed). A listed ID counts only as its own word in a test's printed name (for example, a test titled `TC-4a` does not show `TC-4`: title it `TC-4 (a)`). TC-4 appears only inside: ✖ TC-4a initial position: ... Title each test so its listed ID stands alone.` The `--verbose` hint is kept only for IDs with no hit at all.
- The matching rule is one constant, `shiploop_prompts.ID_WORD_RULE`. It is reused in `COUNT_RULE`, `red_lines`, the test-author duty and the step-plan duty, so it is worded once.
- The strict match stays (TC-4 is still not shown by TC-40). The fifteen-line output tail under the bullet is left alone.

A5 (floors). The model's `min_tests` is only a first guess. ShipLoop now also refuses a run that ran fewer tests than the most any accepted run of the same command ran for the same work item. The change is an additive refusal on an existing status. Built as follows:
- New `shiploop_test_loop.accepted_counts(root, state, work_item, action)` derives the floor from the item's own `tests/<action>-verify<N>.md` records. It reads only `passed` records, and only runs with status `passed` or `red` whose output was counted. It looks only at actions in `state["history"]` after the item's latest accepted step plan, plus the current action. This is the same derivation as `navigator.implement_progress`.
- `verify()` converts an otherwise accepted run below the floor to `too-few-tests`, so it counts toward the 7-refused-run cap. It records an optional `accepted_ran` on any run that had a floor.
- The `too-few-tests` branch of `_explain` names both numbers and the exit. If the floor is higher than the plan's `min_tests`, it says "an earlier run of this command that ShipLoop accepted for this item (at least M)... Restore the tests that were removed or now skip... report revise naming what was removed and why, and the redone step plan starts the count again". Otherwise it keeps the old step-plan text.
- A revise lowers the floor because the revised step plan becomes the newest `step-plan` history row, which puts every earlier record out of scope.
- Interactions with the other runs:
  - The test-author probe is the first accepted observation, not test-red. The probe record is `passed` with status `red` (Checkers verify3 holds 23 and 16, the same as test-red).
  - Test-red holds the floor and `red_na` runs are handled the same way, because the conversion applies to `passed` and `red`.
  - Refused records never set a floor.
- Dropped from the proposal:
  - Filling a floor into recorded commands.
  - Outer stages (`system-test`, `release-verify`) and the end-of-work review. They have no revise to lower a floor, and a union across items would create a dead end, for example a refactor item that merges old tests.
  - A run-wide key (replaced by per-item, per-step-plan scope).

Evidence the design is sound:
- A replay over six real runs (Sonnet and Grok, Battleship and Checkers, round 1 and 2, including a two-item run) produced 0 refusals. Counts only ever grew.
- The ratchet would hold 100% of actual where the model's floors were 43-89%.
- 18 new tests: 13 fail on unchanged code (11 in `test/shiploop-test-loop.test.py`, 2 in `test/shiploop-test-counts.test.py`) and 5 are guards that pass on it. 9 mutation checks are all caught.
- The full `test/shiploop-test-loop.test.py` suite passes: 97 tests, against 81 on unchanged code.
- The packet-completeness, status-display, guidance, delegation, e2e (350 tests), chain and navigator suites pass.

Three corrections to the brief:
1. The first observation is the test-author probe, not the test-red total.
2. SPEC S-9 says a check "that ran nothing" is not a pass. It does not say "ran less". The anchors are S-9 and S-5 (reruns of recorded checks belong to the script).
3. Round-3 acceptance criterion (5) must drop "every regression and consumer command carries a floor". Say instead: "every inner rerun is refused below the highest count accepted since the item's latest step plan, with both numbers; consumer and outer commands are not floored (known limit)".
design.for_against:
FOR:
- Both candidates fit the SPEC. S-9 and S-5: a script decides reruns of recorded checks from observable state. S-4: the model should not learn an engine rule by reading source (Checkers made four source-reading calls and nine calls in total).
- The round-1 rule "act if the gap recurs" is met for A5: 4 of 4 runs, with floors at 43-89% of actual.
- The derivation reuses existing history, records and the revise route, so there is no new state key.
- The replay shows 0 false refusals on six runs.
- Production change is about 117 insertions and 17 deletions across `SKILL.md`, `shiploop_prompts.py`, `shiploop_test_counts.py` and `shiploop_test_loop.py`.
- Packet growth is 149-433 characters per packet. The kept-head window is unchanged.
- The refusal gives both numbers and the exit, as the lens asked.

AGAINST / CAUTIONS:
- No run actually deleted a test, so A5 closes a latent gap rather than a failure seen in a run. It is justified by the owner's own "act on recurrence" rule and by S-9 fidelity.
- A deliberate removal costs a revise. At `test-green`, `regression` and `static-checks` a revise needs a stopped loop packet or the 7-refusal cap (`remedy_open` and `check_loop_packet`), so restoring the tests is the expected path. A revise resets the floors of all the item's commands, not just the removed one.
- A5 does not cover the outer stages or the end-of-work review, so an Improve review that deletes tests is not caught. It also does not cover tests removed before the first accepted run (the baseline stage's counts are model-recorded). Both are known limits, written into the docs and the module docstring.
- A1 was seen in 1 of 6 runs. The printed hint was wrong whatever the frequency, and the fix does not loosen the gate.

State the rule once as `shiploop_prompts.ID_WORD_RULE` and reuse it in `COUNT_RULE`, `red_lines`, `DUTIES['test-author']` and `DUTIES['step-plan']`. Strict matching stays. Seen once in six runs, but the printed `--verbose` hint was wrong for that cause whatever the frequency.

Add `accepted_counts` and a conversion in `verify()` to `too-few-tests` with the optional `accepted_ran` on the run. Scope is per work item, from its latest accepted step plan, inner stages only. The first observation is the test-author probe. A revise lowers it by resetting scope. Add `RATCHET_RULE` to the loop-stage, rerun-stage and test-red packets; no outer stages. No new state key, no fill-a-floor, no cross-item, outer-stage or end-of-work floor. Needs an adversarial evaluation before coding, as noted, but the replay over six runs found 0 false refusals and the prototype passed all nine mutation checks.

`accepted_counts(root, state, work_item, action) -> {command: highest ran}`. Return {} for an empty `work_item`. Take `plan, _ = _step_plan(state, work_item)` and `start` = the history index of that action (default -1). Scan the actions of history rows after `start` whose `workitem` equals the item, plus the current `action`. For each `tests/<action>-verify<N>.md` (via `_verify_count` and `verify_path`), keep only records with `passed`, and in them runs with status `passed` or `red` and an int `counts.ran`. This is the `implement_progress` pattern.

Before the command loop compute `floors = accepted_counts(...) if stage not in OUTER_SOURCES else {}`. After `run.update(judge(...))`, if `floors.get(row['command'])` is set, record `run['accepted_ran']`. If the status is `passed` or `red`, the counts are present and ran is below the floor, set status `too-few-tests`. A failing disposition, so it counts toward `MAX_REFUSED_RUNS`. Module docstring: add the paragraph on the floor and its limits.

`too-few-tests`: if `accepted_ran` is higher than the plan's `min_tests`, name the earlier accepted run and both numbers, say "Restore the tests that were removed or now skip", and name revise as the exit for a deliberate removal. Otherwise keep the step-plan wording. `ids-missing`: use the `ids_inside` branch (rule, quoted line, rename example, no `--verbose`) for IDs with a hit, keep the old remedy for IDs without one, and name both when they differ.

`COUNT_RULE` includes `guidance.ID_WORD_RULE`. New `RATCHET_RULE` (exported in `__all__`): "A run must also run at least as many tests as the most any earlier run of the same command that ShipLoop accepted for this item has run since its latest step plan, so a test removed or newly skipped is refused. To drop a test on purpose, report revise with the reason: the redone step plan starts the count again." `render_lines` (test-green, regression) prints `COUNT_RULE` then `RATCHET_RULE`. `rerun_lines` prints `RATCHET_RULE` unless `stage in OUTER_SOURCES`. `red_lines` carries `ID_WORD_RULE` and `RATCHET_RULE`. These packet lines sit after the status block, so the kept-head window is untouched.

corrections: A1, required: `shiploop_test_counts.named()['inside']` takes the first non-skip line containing the ID as a plain substring (`test_id in line`). An ID that never ran but is a numeric prefix of another test's ID therefore gets a false hit. Reproduced on the prototype: ids ['TC-1','TC-3'] against output titles `TC-10`, `TC-13`, `TC-2` give `inside={'TC-1': '✔ TC-10 a (1ms)'}`. The refusal then says 'TC-1 appears only inside: ✔ TC-10 ... Title each test so its listed ID stands alone' and drops the select-and-print remedy for that ID, which is a wrong remedy in the common TC-n scheme. The prototype's own test pins the bug (`counts.named('✔ TC-40 big (1ms)\n', ['TC-4'])['inside'] == {'TC-4': ...}`). Fix: if the ID ends in a digit, a line counts as inside only when the next character is not a digit (so `TC-4a` is inside, `TC-40` is not). Flip that assertion to `{}` and add a TC-1 versus TC-10 test through `judge` and `_explain`. My mutant with this rule is caught only by that pinning test, so nothing else covers it.

A5, required: the 'report revise' advice is false at the three loop stages. Both the `too-few-tests` branch of `_explain` and `RATCHET_RULE` say 'report revise' with no condition. Through the real gate on the prototype, a revise submitted right after a floor refusal at test-green is refused ('a complete test loop reports outcome done', then 'list the saved terminal packet in evidence_refs'). At static-checks it is refused ('a complete quality loop reports outcome done'). Revise opens there only after 7 refused runs (`remedy_open`) or with a stopped Until Loop packet (`quality.check_loop_packet`). It is free at test-author, test-red, test-refine (accepted, checked), verify and integration-verify. Fix: branch the `_explain` sentence on `stage in STAGES or stage == quality.STAGE`, the condition `verify` already uses in its could-not-run text. At those stages say 'restore the tests; revise opens at the Nth refused run or when the loop stops'. Make `RATCHET_RULE` defer to the attempts line instead of promising revise. Add a fail-first test through the gate at test-green: floor refusal, revise refused with the loop message, revise accepted after 7 refusals.

A5, decision needed before coding: `DUTIES['test-refine']` tells the model to 'Reconcile the original clause/case inventory: explain every removed or narrowed case'. The prototype's test-refine packet prints that sentence next to `RATCHET_RULE` (checked in the rendered packet), and a removal there is refused with revise (a full item redo, 1 of MAX_REVISES=2) as the only exit. Recommended smallest fix, with no new state key: do not apply the floor at test-refine, and start the count again from the item's latest accepted test-refine (scope start = the later of the latest step plan and the latest accepted test-refine). Later stages are then held to the count test-refine accepted. The alternative is to amend the duty so a removed case is a plan change (revise). Either way the packet must not carry both.

A5, evidence wording and decision: replace 'counts only ever grew, 0 false refusals' with 'unmeasured for brownfield'. I replayed every run with verify records under /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs (20 runs, including the two-item and revised runs) and scanned every record, refused ones too: no count ever dropped. All 20 are greenfield, where tests are only added; the round-2 analysis itself records both round-2 cases as 0-baseline-test. The exposed case is untested: implement may edit tests, and removing or replacing obsolete tests there drops the count below the test-author probe taken before implement. The refusal then lands at test-green after a whole Until Loop, and its only exit is the 7-refusal or stopped-loop revise.
